html:
On 25 July 1898 US troops landed at Guanica on the south coast of Puerto Rico, during the Spanish-American War. They met little resistance, and fighting ended within weeks when an armistice was signed.

Puerto Rico had just won self government from Spain under the Charter of Autonomy of 1897, and its new cabinet had met only days before the landing.

Under the Treaty of Paris, Spain ceded the island to the United States. It became an unincorporated territory: owned by the US but not fully part of it. Its people were made US citizens by the Jones Act in 1917, but they still cannot vote for president. The question of status has dominated the island's politics ever since.
